intro.line: Dominaria, before the long winter. Two brothers are building a war.

finale.line: The Sylex. It ends the war.
It was never just me, brother. Someone else was listening.

battles.title: The First Summons
battles.blurb: You wake in a forest that has never seen a planeswalker. Its archers have their bows up already.

scene.line: Stop. You came out of the air.
Things that come out of the air don't usually leave.
Show us what you are. Call something.

villainScene.line: Something fell out of the sky into our forest.
Eyes on it. If it calls one beast, we call ten.

villain.big: The forest answers us, not you.
villain.win: Go back to wherever you fell from.
villain.loss: Fine. The forest will remember you.

battles.title: The Goblin King's Toll
battles.blurb: A mountain pass with a toll and a king who collects it. His army is big, loud and stuck on the ground.

scene.line: Halt! This pass belongs to the king.
I am the king.
Toll is everything you've got. Pay or get stomped.
...Why is your stuff flying? Nobody said flying was allowed.

villainScene.line: Big toll today, boys. Biggest ever.
If it flies, throw rocks at it. Rocks fly too. Sort of.

villain.big: Look at THAT one. That one's mine.
villain.loss: Next time, nets. Lots of nets.

battles.title: Knights at the Ford
battles.blurb: Two knights have held the same river crossing for years. Today one of them finally wants it settled.

scene.line: Every morning, you. Every evening, you.
Every morning, you lose.
Not today. Today I brought a witness.
Then let them see how it's done. Watch the first blow. It's the only one that matters.

villainScene.line: Years at this ford. Every morning, the same white armour.
Today it ends. No prayers, no tricks. Just steel.

hero.low: I've held this ford through worse.
hero.loss: Go on, cross. Just this once.

battles.title: The Djinn of the Bottle
battles.blurb: A rift drops you into Rabiah, the world of the Thousand and One Nights, at the feet of a djinn who is bored of granting wishes.

scene.line: A new face! Do you know how long it's been since I had a new face?
Every visitor wishes. Gold, wives, kingdoms. Tiresome.
You will not wish. You will duel. Win, and I'll show you the way home.
Lose, and you stay. I collect people.

villainScene.line: A rift-walker. I've collected kings, but never one of those.
Make it a long duel. I want to savour this one.

villain.big: Behold the gift of the djinn.
villain.loss: Go, then! The rift is that way. Visit.

battles.title: Argoth Burns
battles.blurb: The rift spits you out on Argoth, a forest island. Two brothers are cutting it down to build their war.

scene.line: You smell of the rift. Good. You're not one of his.
Urza takes our trees for fuel. Mishra takes them for spite. Both take.
The island has the finest timber in the world. That makes it a resource.
I have a war to win. Sentiment is a luxury.
Then we will be very expensive.

villainScene.line: Titania thinks the trees are sacred. Mishra thinks they're spite.
I think they're fuel. And I am out of fuel.

battles.title: The Efreet of Serendib
battles.blurb: The rift flickers back to Rabiah. Sindbad needs a crew, and the island of Serendib has its own guardian.

scene.line: You again! The rift-walker. I've a ship, a map and no crew. You'll do.
Serendib is not for sailors.
Everything is for sailors, friend. That's what the sea is for.
Then the sea may have what's left of you.

villainScene.line: Another sailor, another promise of treasure.
Serendib has outlasted a thousand ships. It can outlast one more.

hero.low: I've been shipwrecked six times. Seven's fine.

battles.title: Factories at Kroog
battles.blurb: The war comes to Kroog, Urza's capital. His apprentice holds the walls against Mishra's cruellest engineer.

scene.line: Tawnos! Still holding the master's tools?
Still taking people apart, Ashnod?
Only to see how they work. You'd do the same if he let you.
Help me hold the factories. If Kroog falls, nothing stops her.
Oh, bring your friend. I've never taken a planeswalker apart.

villainScene.line: Kroog's walls, Tawnos's toys, and a planeswalker to open up.
Mishra wants the factories. I want to see how everything works inside.

villain.loss: Next time I'm bringing the big altar.

battles.title: Mishra's War Machine
battles.blurb: Thirty years of war, two halves of one stone, and two brothers meeting on the same battlefield at last.

scene.line: Brother. You look old.
You look like you've made friends you shouldn't have.
Friends? They listen. That's more than you ever did.
Give me the Mightstone, Mishra.
Come and take it. You always do.

villainScene.line: They told me I'd finally be better than you.

hero.win: It's over. Give it to me.

villain.start: Just like when we were boys.
villain.big: Look what I made without you!
villain.low: You always win. Why do you always win?

battles.title: How Do You Stop This Deck?
battles.blurb: Under the snow, a deck from before anything was forbidden. It draws you cards until they kill you.

scene.line: After the Sylex, the snow. Under the snow, something older than the war.
Subject: How do you stop this deck?
Take seven cards. Take seven more. Every one of them hurts.
Nothing on Dominaria plays like that.
Nothing on Dominaria was ever told no.
By your second turn the damage is bad enough. Ask anyone who answered the thread.

villainScene.line: They asked how to stop me. Nobody had an answer.

after.line: Re: How do you stop this deck?
Break the Vises. Keep your hand small. Hit hard.
A week later, the first cards were restricted.

hero.low: Too many cards. Too much pain.

villain.win: How do you stop this deck? You don't.
